# Architecture · project standards (detail)

<!-- docs/standards/architecture.md · Generated by project-init v0.4.1 on 2026-11-17.
On-demand reference: not loaded automatically. The project's architecture rules are in CLAUDE.md ("Code design"). -->

## Modular monolith
- **Rule:** One Streamlit app with a layered package. Split into services only with a recorded reason in an ADR.
- **Why:** Services add network, data and operations complexity this project doesn't need.
- **Decision:** Modular monolith (ADR 0002).
- **Status:** Enforced by the import-linter contracts in `pyproject.toml`.

## Clear boundaries
- **Rule:** Domain logic imports no framework, provider SDK or other project package.
- **Why:** The core stays testable, and infrastructure can change without touching business rules.
- **Status:** Enforced (import-linter: "domain imports no other project package").

## No shared state between sessions
- **Rule:** App instances keep no visitor data outside each visitor's own session. Nothing is written to disk.
- **Why:** On a shared process, anything global can leak between visitors.
- **Status:** Enforced as a security rule (`.claude/rules/security.md`); SPEC section 6.

## Synchronous or asynchronous calls
- **Rule:** Model calls are synchronous inside the Streamlit run, with a progress display and a timeout per call.
- **Why:** See ADR 0004.
- **Decision:** Synchronous calls with timeouts, over streaming or background jobs (ADR 0004).
- **Status:** Enforced for new LLM code (`.claude/rules/ai-llm.md`).

## Quality attributes drive the design
- **Rule:** Major trade-offs are justified against the three quality attributes in ADR 0002: security of visitor keys, time to first report, and running cost.
- **Why:** Naming the priorities makes trade-offs explicit.
- **Status:** Documented in ADR 0002 (Accepted).

## Architecture style chosen explicitly
- **Rule:** The style and the rejected options are recorded.
- **Why:** Styles have very different costs; choosing by habit is expensive.
- **Status:** Documented in SPEC section 7 and ADR 0002.

## Effort proportional to reversibility
- **Rule:** Hard-to-reverse choices (data model, report schema, provider, hosting, licence, a paid tool) get an ADR. Easy-to-reverse ones are decided quickly.
- **Why:** Over-analysing reversible choices wastes time; under-analysing irreversible ones creates years of cost.
- **Status:** Adopting (CLAUDE.md "Decisions" in the project standards block).

## Anti-corruption layer for AI providers
- **Rule:** Provider SDKs are used only in `llm/`, behind the `LLMClient` protocol. The rest of the code never sees a provider's types.
- **Why:** Provider models change on someone else's schedule; one adapter contains the change.
- **Status:** Documented in CLAUDE.md. An import-linter contract that forbids `anthropic` and `openai` outside `llm` is planned for M4.
